videos.script: Horta takes one random sample of forty orders. The mean basket comes out at eighty-two reais and thirty-nine centavos. {{sample}} Is the true mean of all orders eighty-two thirty-nine? Almost certainly not exactly. A different forty orders would have given a different number. {{different}} The question is how different. Within a real or two? Within twenty? {{how}} Lesson eleven answered it in principle. Sample means wobble around the true mean with a spread of sigma over root n. This lesson puts a number on that wobble from the one sample you have. It is called the standard error. {{se}} Then it builds a range around the sample mean: about two standard errors each side. That range is a confidence interval, and here it runs from about fifty-seven reais to about one hundred and eight. {{interval}} You will also learn what the ninety-five percent in a confidence interval means, because most people who quote it get it wrong. And you will work out how many customers a survey needs, before anybody is asked a single question. {{survey}}
